thread:
marta: Quick heads-up — saw a big p99 jump on chatstream after enabling mb=1 for streaming. Figured we should triage before canarying more customers.
ron: Link to the run + numbers?
marta: Paste from profiler: streaming mb=1 -> p95=120ms, p99=840ms, KVCACHE_MISS=45%. Non-streaming completions (mb=8) -> p95=95ms, p99=220ms, KVCACHE_MISS=12%.
lee: Woah. Kernel switch rate up too?
marta: Yes. kernel_switches/sec roughly doubled on the streaming pool. Traces show lots of short-lived attention_kernel_fallback activations.
ron: Hypothesis: tiny microbatches cause frequent shape/context changes so selector toggles kernels and KV cache churns. Tail work increases.
lee: Makes sense. Also tiny mb => less opportunity to amortize kernel warmup / kv cache locality.
marta: I grabbed a perf trace snippet: `TRACE: req=0x7f2, kernel=attention_v2 -> attention_tail_fallback (latency 37ms), KVCACHE_MISS at step 3` repeated many times. perf-bot: traced as TRC-20260301-71, correlated with KVCACHE_MISS spikes.
ron: Two levers to try: 1) prefetch on new stream start to warm KV, 2) hysteresis in kernel selector so we don't flip per tiny batch. Also 3) micro-coalescing delay (e.g., 8-10ms) to collect a couple of requests.
lee: Prefetch seems attractive for strict-latency streaming customers (can't add delay). Coalescing helps throughput but adds tail-latency risk if we wait. Kernel hysteresis is low-cost.
marta: Experimented locally: prefetch=8 tokens + mb=1 => p99 dropped from 840ms to ~290ms, p95 unchanged. CPU up ~5% and GPU mem ops + small.
ron: Nice win. Any effect on kernel_switch_rate?
marta: Reduced by ~40% because warming prevented fallback path in many cases.
lee: For hysteresis: propose selector requires a sustained shape signal for 200ms before switching kernel, and at least 2 consecutive batches with same token-length distribution. Might add small extra tail for cold shapes but reduces oscillation.
ron: Sounds reasonable. For coalescing: delay choice depends on SLO. Many streaming customers have 200-500ms tail budgets, so 10ms delay likely acceptable; others not. We should make it per-tenant config.
marta: Proposed A/B: Variant A = prefetch(8) + kernel-hysteresis(on). Variant B = coalescing delay=10ms + kernel-hysteresis(off). Measure p95/p99, KVCACHE_MISS, kernel_switch_rate, tokens/sec.
lee: Also measure overhead on CPU/GPU and cost per token.
ron: I'll add dashboard tiles: KVCACHE_MISS, KVCACHE_HIT_RATE, KERNEL_SWITCH_RATE, p95/p99, cpu%, tokens/sec. Link when done.
marta: Running canary tonight: 2h baseline (current prod), 2h variant A on pool A, 2h variant B on pool B, then rollback. I'll attach traces. Will disable autoscale for the window to keep stable. ops-bot: reminder sent to oncall to expect canary.
ron: One more thought — for non-streaming completions the best is larger microbatch (mb>=8). Could we auto-route completions to a bulk pool and streams to a stream-optimized pool with different defaults?
lee: We already have pool flavors but routing needs to be workload-aware. Could add a simple heuristic: if request has streaming flag -> stream-pool, else bulk-pool. Might help.
marta: Going to include that in the run: stream-pool gets prefetch + hysteresis, bulk-pool gets coalescing=none + larger mb.
ron: Great. Post results in the thread and mark any follow-ups. :thumbsup:
marta: Will do. Posting initial trace link once processing finishes.
lee: Thanks — this feels like a clean path to reduce tail without sacrificing throughput.
perf-bot: TRC-20260301-71 analysis queued. Expect follow-up in ~30m.
marta: (later) quick update: variant A p99=310ms, variant B p99=420ms, baseline 840ms. KVCACHE_MISS down 38% on A, kernel_switch_rate down 35%. Will run another longer window tomorrow to confirm.
ron: Nice! Let's convert prefetch+hysteresis into a default for stream-pool and document tradeoffs.
lee: I'll open a PR for kernel selector hysteresis and add unit tests.
marta: Thanks team.
